content: Aggrenox Extended-Release Capsules are prescribed to reduce the risk of stroke in patients who have previously experienced a stroke caused by a blood clot in the brain. It is also used to lower the risk of stroke in patients who have had transient ischemic attacks (TIAs), which are often referred to as warning strokes or mini-strokes that cause stroke-like symptoms without lasting damage. Aggrenox is a combination antiplatelet medication that works by preventing the formation of blood clots. Do not use Aggrenox Extended-Release Capsules if: You are allergic to any ingredient in the medication. You have bleeding disorders. You are under 18 years old and have the flu, chickenpox, or shingles. You have had a severe allergic reaction (e.g., rash, hives, difficulty breathing, dizziness) to aspirin or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) such as ibuprofen, naproxen, or celecoxib. If any of these conditions apply to you, contact your doctor or healthcare provider immediately. Before using Aggrenox Extended-Release Capsules: Inform your doctor or pharmacist if you have any medical conditions, especially if: You are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. You are taking any prescription or nonprescription medications, herbal preparations, or dietary supplements. You have allergies to medicines, foods, or other substances. You have asthma, peptic ulcers, stomach problems, liver issues, a blood clotting disorder, the flu, chickenpox, shingles, hives, rash, intense itching, Kawasaki syndrome, nasal tumors, vitamin K deficiency, or a history of bleeding in the brain. Certain medications may interact with Aggrenox, such as pyridostigmine, diuretics (e.g., hydrochlorothiazide), probenecid, or sulfinpyrazone, as their effectiveness may be reduced. This is not a complete list of potential interactions. Consult your healthcare provider to determine if Aggrenox may interact with other medications you are taking. Always check with your healthcare provider before starting, stopping, or changing the dose of any medication. How to use Aggrenox Extended-Release Capsules: Take the medication exactly as directed by your doctor. Follow the dosing instructions on the label. Swallow the capsules whole with or without food. Do not break, crush, or chew them before swallowing. Avoid lying down for 15 to 30 minutes after taking the medication to prevent irritation to the esophagus. Do not substitute this form of aspirin for any other form of aspirin. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as possible. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at once. Contact your healthcare provider if you have any questions about how to use this medication. Important safety information: Aggrenox may cause dizziness, which can be worsened by alcohol or certain medications. Use caution when driving or performing tasks that require alertness until you know how the medication affects you. Dizziness or fainting may occur, especially with alcohol, hot weather, exercise, or fever. To prevent these effects, sit or stand up slowly, particularly in the morning. Lie down if you feel dizzy or faint. If you consume more than three alcoholic drinks per day, consult your doctor before taking Aggrenox, as it may increase the risk of serious stomach ulcers or bleeding. High doses, long-term use, smoking, or alcohol consumption can heighten these risks. Taking the medication with food will not reduce these risks. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience severe stomach or back pain, black or tarry stools, vomit that looks like blood or coffee grounds, or unusual weight gain or swelling. Aspirin has been associated with Reye syndrome, a serious illness. Do not give Aggrenox to children or teenagers with the flu, chickenpox, or a viral infection. Consult your doctor with any concerns. Inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking Aggrenox before undergoing any medical, dental, or emergency procedures. Diabetic patients should monitor their blood sugar levels closely, as Aggrenox may affect them. Consult your doctor before adjusting the dose of your diabetes medication. Use Aggrenox with caution in elderly patients, as they may be more sensitive to its effects. Aggrenox is not recommended for use in children, as its safety and effectiveness have not been established. If you become pregnant, contact your doctor to discuss the benefits and risks of using Aggrenox during pregnancy. It is not recommended during the last trimester, as it may harm the fetus. Aggrenox is found in breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding to discuss potential risks to your baby. Possible side effects: Most people experience no or minor side effects. Common side effects include constipation, diarrhea, dizziness, headache, heartburn, indigestion, and stomach pain. Contact your doctor if these persist or become bothersome. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience severe side effects, such as: Severe allergic reactions (rash, hives, itching, difficulty swallowing or breathing, chest tightness, swelling of the hands, mouth, face, lips, eyes, throat, or tongue). Bloody or black, tarry stools. Chest pain, convulsions, dark urine, pale stools, hoarseness, memory loss, nausea, severe stomach pain, stroke, unusual fatigue, vomiting (with or without blood), or yellowing of the skin or eyes. This is not a complete list of side effects. Contact your doctor or healthcare provider for medical advice about side effects. You may report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088. In case of overdose: If an overdose is suspected, contact the American Association of Poison Control Centers at 1-800-222-1222, your local poison control center, or an emergency room immediately. Symptoms of overdose may include dizziness, rapid heartbeat, flushing, restlessness, ringing in the ears, sweating, or weakness. Proper storage: Store Aggrenox at room temperature (59–77°F or 15–25°C) in a tightly closed container. Keep it away from heat, moisture, and light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it out of reach of children and pets.
